task: Review StudioDisplayName Unicode visibility, control handling, readable fallback selection and meaningful Unicode preservation.
scope_exclusions: Source, tree, branch and ref modifications

checks.result: Read AGENTS.md, all eight mandated startup documents and m02-m03-code-v2; M03 remains active. No milestone promotion inferred.
Reviewed at most 321 inspected source scalars, 80-character/320-scalar/1280-byte caps, ellipsis reservations and requested-limit clamping; no additional defect identified.
Unsafe categories and explicit bidi-control ranges are rejected by newInput and replaced for display; tests cover representative line/control/bidi inputs. Tests were read, not run.

Existing assertions cover combining accents, Arabic/Hebrew/CJK, ZWNJ/ZWJ, variation selectors, Indic joining and emoji families; hasDisplayContent gates an entire name without stripping meaningful embedded formatting.

checks.method: Static trace with U+2800 input and primary Unicode documentation
checks.result: One P2 issue: U+2800 is a blank symbol outside both rejected visibility properties, so a blank-only name is considered display content. Runtime reproduction was not performed.

findings.title: Braille blank-only names bypass empty-name validation and visible fallback

reproduction.predicted_actual: All three paths retain U+2800: it is not whitespace, is not default-ignorable, and is not rejected by isUnsafe. The label path sees a nonempty string and bypasses the fallback.
reproduction.expected: Treat a string containing only BRAILLE PATTERN BLANK and other non-content scalars as empty for new input; display should return empty so label chooses its visible fallback.

findings.impact: A user can enter a visually blank name and retained blank-only names produce a blank UI label instead of the contextual fallback. This undermines the readable-name contract without affecting storage integrity.
findings.recommendation: Make U+2800 non-content in hasDisplayContent, without removing it from otherwise meaningful names. Add tests for a single/repeated braille blank, mixtures with whitespace/default-ignorable scalars, label fallback, and preservation inside visible braille or ordinary text.
evidence: hasDisplayContent accepts any scalar that is neither whitespace nor default-ignorable.
Existing invisible-name tests enumerate default-ignorable fillers but do not include U+2800.
Unicode chart describes U+2800 as BRAILLE PATTERN BLANK and says it is rendered as a fixed-width blank in many fonts but does not act as a space.
findings.validation_needed: Run focused Swift regression tests and confirm the label in the app's supported font. No claim of observed iOS rendering or test execution is made.

limitations: Host unavailable: no local checkout, local files, shell commands, repository scripts, Swift tests, builds or app runtime were used.
Review was limited to the pinned remotely fetched source/test files and mandatory startup/acceptance guidance.
Unicode rendering impact is source-derived and supported by primary Unicode documentation; actual platform font output was not observed.
No source, tree, commit, branch or ref was modified; only this unreferenced report blob is uploaded.
